— one watcher for the in-game
ext_trigger
files, fanned out to print, exec or TCP
Entry points
Core · watch, gate, dedup, fan out
State
External
`sof_export_fire.py --root <sof> --print` — flags: `--trigger`, `--exec`, `--serve`
`TriggerWatcher(root, on_event=...)` — the library API, one file, no install
a TCP subscriber — one `subscribe` line, then JSON events"
`main()` — builds the hook list: print · exec · `server.publish`
`watchdog` `Observer`, recursive on the SoF root; handler on created + modified
path must hold `ext_trigger`, end `.cfg`, match `user-(\d+)`; `last.cfg` skipped
per path 1 s, then a 0.5 s settle sleep so a half-written cfg is not read
`set "key" "value"` lines, latin-1, no name means no event
`TriggerEvent` — name, seq, slot, args 1-3, hostname, map, data_dir
`_last_seq` per path — a redelivery only counts when the seq advances
`print_event` · `exec_hook_factory` (`subprocess`) · `EventServer.publish`
`user-<port>/sofplus/data/ext_trigger/*.cfg` — one file per trigger name, overwritten
`last.cfg` — alias of the newest fire, never read by the watcher
`_last_seq` / `_last_time` — plain dicts in memory, lost on restart
`ext_trigger.func` (from `sof-profiles`) — the in-game half, writes `<name>.cfg`
the running SoF server process — fires a trigger, bumps `_ext_trigger_seq`
`sof-discord-bot` — the reference consumer, subscribes over TCP
`systemd/sof-export-fire.service` — ships with the bot, venv + `--serve`
